title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
problem: Large language models suffer from hallucinations and factual errors, and while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) addresses this by augmenting inputs with retrieved documents, it heavily relies on retrieval quality and performance degrades significantly when retrieval fails or returns inaccurate results.
contributions: Proposes CRAG with a lightweight retrieval evaluator to assess document quality and trigger different knowledge retrieval actions
Extends retrieval with large-scale web searches when static corpus returns suboptimal documents
Designs decompose-then-recompose algorithm to filter irrelevant information from retrieved documents
Demonstrates plug-and-play integration with existing RAG approaches including Self-RAG
Shows significant performance improvements on four datasets covering short and long-form generation tasks

title: R2AG: Incorporating Retrieval Information into Retrieval Augmented Generation
problem: A semantic gap exists between LLMs and retrievers due to differences in their training objectives and architectures. This misalignment forces LLMs to passively accept documents from retrievers without fully understanding them, burdening LLMs with distinguishing relevant documents using inherent knowledge.
method: Retrieval information integration with R2-Former and retrieval-aware prompting
contributions: Proposes R2AG framework that bridges the semantic gap between retrievers and LLMs by incorporating retrieval information
Introduces R2-Former architecture to capture nuanced retrieval features
Designs retrieval-aware prompting strategy to integrate retrieval information into LLM generation
Demonstrates effectiveness across five datasets while supporting low-resource scenarios with frozen LLMs and retrievers
Shows that retrieval information serves as an anchor to aid generation and mitigate hallucination
key_results: Extensive experiments across five datasets validate the effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency of R2AG
Retrieval information serves as an anchor to aid LLMs in the generation process

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique Through Self-Reflection
problem: Large language models often produce responses containing factual inaccuracies despite their capabilities. While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) helps reduce factual errors, it indiscriminately retrieves a fixed number of passages regardless of necessity or relevance, which can diminish LM versatility or lead to unhelpful generation.
method: Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation with reflection tokens
contributions: Introduces Self-RAG framework that trains a single LM to adaptively retrieve passages on-demand using reflection tokens
Enables controllable LM behavior during inference to tailor responses to diverse task requirements
Generates both retrieval tokens and critique tokens to decide when retrieval is needed and evaluate generation quality
Significantly outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on open-domain QA, reasoning, and fact verification tasks
Improves factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generation
key_results: Self-RAG (7B and 13B parameters) outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks
Shows significant gains in improving factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generations

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
problem: Large language models often generate outputs that are untruthful, toxic, or not aligned with user intent, because the language modeling objective (predicting the next token) differs from the objective of following user instructions helpfully and safely. This paper addresses how to align language models with user intent on a wide range of tasks.
method: Supervised learning fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning from human feedback
contributions: Demonstrates that a 1.3B parameter InstructGPT model outperforms a 175B GPT-3 model in human evaluations despite having 100x fewer parameters
Shows that fine-tuning with human feedback improves model truthfulness and reduces toxic output generation
Achieves minimal performance regressions on public NLP datasets while improving instruction-following
Proposes a scalable approach combining supervised learning on labeler demonstrations with RLHF on ranked outputs
Provides evidence that fine-tuning with human feedback is a promising direction for aligning language models with human intent
key_results: Outputs from 1.3B InstructGPT (PPO-ptx) are preferred to outputs from 175B GPT-3 in human evaluations on API prompt distribution
InstructGPT models show improvements in truthfulness and reductions in toxic output generation
Minimal performance regressions on public NLP datasets

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
problem: As AI systems become more capable, there is a need to develop methods for training harmless AI assistants that do not rely on extensive human supervision. This paper addresses how to train AI systems that remain helpful, honest, and harmless through self-improvement mechanisms, without requiring human labels identifying harmful outputs.
method: Constitutional AI with self-critique and reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF)
contributions: Introduces Constitutional AI (CAI), a method for training harmless AI assistants using a constitution of principles rather than extensive human feedback
Proposes a two-stage training process combining supervised learning with self-critique/revision and reinforcement learning from AI feedback
Demonstrates that AI models can evaluate and provide feedback on their own outputs to improve harmlessness
Shows that chain-of-thought reasoning can improve transparency and performance of AI decision-making
Enables training of non-evasive AI assistants that engage with harmful queries by explaining objections rather than refusing

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
problem: Large language models have been predominantly closed-source, limiting community research and responsible development. This work addresses the need for open, well-performing foundation and chat-optimized models that enable the community to build upon and contribute to the responsible development of LLMs.
method: Supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), with safety fine-tuning and red teaming
contributions: Developed and released Llama 2, a collection of pretrained LLMs ranging from 7B to 70B parameters
Created Llama 2-Chat, fine-tuned models optimized for dialogue use cases that outperform open-source chat models on most benchmarks
Provided detailed descriptions of fine-tuning approaches including supervised fine-tuning and RLHF for enabling community development
Implemented comprehensive safety improvements including pretraining data filtering, safety-focused fine-tuning, and red teaming
Demonstrated that Llama 2-Chat may be a suitable substitute for closed-source models based on human evaluations for helpfulness and safety
limitations: Testing conducted to date has been in English and has not covered all scenarios
Potential outputs cannot be predicted in advance and the model may produce inaccurate or objectionable responses to user prompts
Developers should perform safety testing and tuning tailored to their specific applications before deploying Llama 2
Some benchmarks (ASwag and MMLU-Humanities) appear to have benefitted from data contamination in the training data
key_results: Pretrained on 2 trillion tokens of data from publicly available sources
Fine-tuning includes over one million human-annotated examples
Models outperform open-source chat models on most benchmarks tested
Training utilized 3.3M GPU hours of A100-80GB computation with estimated carbon emissions of 539 tCO2eq
